commands.name: attention
commands.summary: The canonical tending primitive: wait until attention is needed, then return a digest with wake reason and next cursor.
commands.description: The canonical tending primitive: wait until attention is needed, then return a digest with wake reason and next cursor. This is the one obvious way to implement an operator loop. Combines wait + digest semantics with cursor handoff for mechanical replay.

parameters.name: attention-timeout
parameters.description: Maximum wait time before returning

parameters.name: attention-poll
parameters.description: Polling interval

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Attention profile: operator, debug, minimal, alerts

parameters.name: attention-condition
parameters.description: Which condition to wait for: attention, action_required, mail_pending

profiles.description: Default profile for operator agents. Shows actionable events and important state changes.

profiles.name: debug
profiles.description: Full verbosity for debugging. Shows all events including debug level.

profiles.name: minimal

cursor_replay.note: Replay uses monotonic cursors with explicit resync instructions on expiration.

operator_boundary.note: Attention feed remains a sensing/actuation surface only; it does not assign work, infer intent, or replace beads, bv, or Agent Mail.

profile_presets.note: Named attention profiles resolve first, then explicit filters narrow or override the effective filter set.

bead_orphaned.note: Unsupported: ntm cannot yet prove orphaned work from observable beads, bv, and agent state without inventing coordination conclusions.

unsupported_conditions.name: bead_orphaned
unsupported_conditions.reason: ntm cannot prove work is orphaned from observable state alone. Agent silence may indicate compaction, deep thinking, rch compilation, or intentional pause — not abandonment. Emitting this signal would produce false positives that erode operator trust.
unsupported_conditions.what_would_change: Agent Mail gains explicit 'bead abandon' or 'bead handoff' messages, giving ntm positive evidence of intent rather than inferring abandonment from silence.

guardrails.name: nervous_system_not_planner
guardrails.rule: ntm emits observable state and executes commands, but it must not invent plans, hidden task graphs, or coordinator conclusions.
guardrails.rationale: The operator agent remains the decision-maker; ntm should sense and act, not pretend to think on the operator's behalf.

guardrails.name: one_obvious_tending_loop
guardrails.rule: Prefer --robot-attention for the steady-state operator loop; use --robot-events for replay/debug and --robot-digest for non-blocking summaries.
guardrails.rationale: This keeps tending simpler than repeated snapshot polling and prevents multiple competing loop patterns.

guardrails.name: cursor_resync_is_explicit
guardrails.rule: When replay is stale or CURSOR_EXPIRED occurs, resync with --robot-snapshot instead of guessing missed history.
guardrails.rationale: Cursor expiry is a retention boundary with explicit recovery semantics, not a reason to fabricate state.

guardrails.name: unsupported_conditions_stay_explicit
guardrails.rule: Unsupported conditions such as bead_orphaned must stay explicit in help and capabilities until ntm can prove them from observable state.
guardrails.rationale: Honest unsupported markers prevent false positives and coordinator-style overreach.
